title: Hopeverse: Naughty Hero v3 (composed transitions, his own sounds)
maker: ElevenLabs Music API on the owner's paid plan

request.prompt: Playful, cheeky yet heroic modern Tamil mass-hero film score for a mischievous little dog who turns out to be the hero, composed and played like a real film composer's cue, not a DJ mix. 112 BPM bouncy swagger groove, D minor with a cheeky lift to F major in the hero section. Signature sound: the dog's own sounds turned into instruments, mixed with broken, processed Carnatic instruments: a real dog bark pitched down and tuned as the deep bass hit on downbeats, a jingling collar bell as the hi-hat, clicking claw taps as the shaker, a squeaky toy squeak tuned into a cheeky lead stab, short panting as a breathy pulse; a glitch-chopped plucked veena riff, mridangam pitched down as bass, ghatam and kanjira as tight playful percussion. Signature motif: a rising 3-note call (root, up a minor third, up to the fifth, the last note held and bent upward) on a gritty synth lead in the first 5 seconds and again at the end. Underneath: warm bouncy synth bass, real cinematic drums played by a drummer, brass section and strings. Vocals: deep male crowd chants 'hey!' and 'ho!' and a short human whistle like calling a dog, no lyrics. Structure with composed transitions, each one different: 0-10 s sneaky tease, tiptoe plucked veena riff and claw taps, the 3-note call. 10-12 s: transition 1, a cheeky pizzicato strings pickup run climbing into the theme, then the only reversed veena swell of the track into one big hit and a crowd 'hey!'. 12-28 s: the bouncy 4-bar main theme on the synth lead, the squeaky-toy stab answering each phrase; on the second pass the melody is varied and climbs higher. 28-32 s: transition 2, the surprise: the band falls away and one lonely bansuri flute plays a sad little 'I am in trouble' phrase for one bar over just the panting pulse, then the low brass answers with the theme in a heroic voice. 32-44 s: the hero turn in F major: the theme on full brass and strings with the drums at full power, call-and-response chants on every bar, a strings counter-melody on top. 44-46 s: transition 3, a real drummer's tom fill and a brass rip, no riser. 46-56 s: everything at full power, the melody now developed into its biggest, highest version, the bark bass hits on every downbeat. 56-60 s: the final hit, then the 3-note call rings out alone on the veena with one cheeky whistle. Something new happens at least every 8 seconds; the drums never thin out in the middle. No white-noise risers or filter sweeps between sections, no build-and-drop, no EDM drops, no stutters, no side-chain pumping, no DJ transitions; clear, tonal, punchy cinematic mix; not childish, a cool cheeky hero.

brief.notes: Jithesh 29 Oct on v2: music really good, but transitions not interesting and sometimes a DJ mix, not a musician's art. v3: rule 9.10, composed transitions, no post tricks.

story: Jithesh's dog: a bit naughty, always up to mischief, but when it matters he is the hero.
human_work: to be added by the owner: melody, take choice, edits, mix
